entry.title: Bounds on chain length with BIP-54 timewarp fixes
entry.summary:
The recent analysis highlights a significant aspect of the current programming strategy where utilizing the timespan limit from the last three timestamps enhances profitability. It has been observed that no other solutions perform as effectively when the timespan is restricted to a minimum of 0.25. This approach appears to exploit a loophole or hack, resulting in a notable gain of 932 blocks.
Further examination reveals an interesting comparison regarding the uniformity of timespan settings across various periods. Specifically, setting every timespan the same incurs a cost of 4,669 blocks, though it constitutes an optimal increase of 7.12% per period. These findings suggest that while standardizing timespans might seem costly, it aligns with achieving a consistent performance improvement. This strategy might be beneficial for enhancing system efficiency over time, despite the initial high block expense.
